cases.requirement: JSON null canonicalizes exactly to the UTF-8 bytes for null with no surrounding whitespace or BOM.
JSON true canonicalizes exactly to true.
JSON false canonicalizes exactly to false.
An empty JSON string canonicalizes exactly to two quotation-mark delimiters.
U+0008, U+0009, U+000A, U+000C, and U+000D use the RFC 8785 predefined JSON escapes b, t, n, f, and r.
ASCII control characters without a predefined short escape use lowercase \uhhhh notation.
Quotation mark and reverse solidus are escaped exactly as required by RFC 8785.
Solidus is not escaped merely as a presentation preference.
Valid non-ASCII Unicode content is preserved as supplied and emitted as UTF-8 after JSON string serialization.
Canonically equivalent Unicode strings in different normalization forms are not normalized or collapsed by M5-002.
A string containing a lone high surrogate fails canonicalization rather than emitting replacement data.
A string containing a lone low surrogate fails canonicalization rather than emitting replacement data.
An empty array canonicalizes exactly to [].
Array element order is preserved exactly and is never sorted by the canonicalizer.
Objects nested inside arrays have their own properties recursively canonicalized while the surrounding array order remains unchanged.
An empty object canonicalizes exactly to {}.
ASCII property names sort lexicographically by raw UTF-16 code-unit values independent of insertion order.
Property sorting uses raw unescaped names, so control characters participate by their underlying UTF-16 code-unit values rather than their escape spelling.
Non-ASCII property ordering follows RFC 8785 UTF-16 code-unit ordering rather than UTF-8 byte order or locale collation.
Property sorting is applied recursively to every nested object regardless of the parent object's original insertion order.
Canonical output contains no insignificant spaces, indentation, line breaks, comments, or trailing commas.
Negative zero canonicalizes to the same number text as zero, namely 0.
Ordinary finite integral binary64 values use RFC 8785/ECMAScript number serialization with no locale-specific separators or suffixes.
The finite binary64 value 1e30 canonicalizes to 1e+30.
cases.evidence: Spec 0054 section 8 and RFC 8785 number serialization.

cases.requirement: The finite binary64 value 0.002 canonicalizes to 0.002.
The finite binary64 value 1e-27 canonicalizes to 1e-27.
RFC 8785 binary64 rounding/serialization samples are reproduced exactly rather than reformatted with host-language decimal preferences.
cases.evidence: Spec 0054 section 8 and RFC 8785 sections 3.2.2.3 / Appendix B.

cases.requirement: NaN presented through a host-language probe fails canonicalization.
Positive Infinity presented through a host-language probe fails canonicalization.
Negative Infinity presented through a host-language probe fails canonicalization.

Host-only values such as undefined, functions, symbols, unmapped BigInt/arbitrary-precision values, Date objects, Map/Set, and non-JSON class instances are rejected rather than silently omitted, stringified, coerced, or converted to null.
A cyclic object or array graph fails canonicalization rather than recursing indefinitely or returning partial bytes.
The canonical artifact is exact UTF-8 bytes with no BOM, trailing newline, NUL terminator, UTF-16/UTF-32 output, or lossy replacement transcoding.
Two semantically equal JSON objects that differ only in property insertion order canonicalize to exactly the same UTF-8 bytes, independent of locale and host map iteration order.
M5-002 produces canonical bytes only and does not compute SHA-256, format digest strings, attach digest fields, build hash chains, or claim tamper evidence.
cases.evidence: Spec 0054 sections 1, 2 and 16; M5-003/M5-004 own digest/hash-chain behavior.

cases.requirement: Protocol-first scope contains only Spec 0054, this corpus, and CURRENT; production/dependency/lockfile/Schema/TCK/HISTORY/roadmap/workflow and M5-003+ changes remain unauthorized until exact-head dual-green.
